title: The Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines
seo_title: Precalculus Law of Sines and Law of Cosines Worksheets (TEKS P.4G, P.4H)
standard_text: P.4G use the Law of Sines in mathematical and real-world problems; P.4H use the Law of Cosines in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines for Texas TEKS P.4G and P.4H: missing sides and angles, triangle area and choosing a law. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Law of Sines: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.
key_sub: Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Law of Sines: asin A = bsin B = csin C. Use it with two angles and a side, or two sides and an angle opposite one of them.
  • Law of Cosines: c2 = a2 + b2 − 2ab cos C. Use it with two sides and the angle between them, or three sides.
  • Area = 12ab sin C.

Examples

Example

a = 7, b = 9, C = 60°

c2 = 49 + 81 − 2(7)(9)(0.5) = 67

Answer: c ≈ 8.2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Pairing a side with the wrong angleSide a is opposite angle A.
Missing the obtuse anglesin B = 0.6 gives B ≈ 36.9° or 143.1°.
+ 2ab cos CThe Law of Cosines subtracts.

faq.q: Does the Law of Cosines work for right triangles?
faq.a: Yes: cos 90° = 0, so it becomes the Pythagorean theorem.

items.q: In △ABC, m∠A = 67°, a = 11 and b = 5. Find m∠B to the nearest tenth of a degree.
items.e: Law of Sines: sin B/b = sin A/a, so sin B = 5 × sin 67° ÷ 11 = 0.4184. m∠B = sin−1(0.4184) = 24.7°. (B is opposite a shorter side, so it is acute.)

You know all three sides of a triangle. Which law finds an angle?
items.e: SSS: rearrange the Law of Cosines to find the cosine of an angle. Law of Cosines.

items.q: You know two sides and the angle between them. Which law finds the third side?
items.e: SAS gives no matching side-angle pair, so use the Law of Cosines. Law of Cosines.

items.q: In the area formula ½ab sin C, where is angle C?
items.e: C must be the included angle, the one between the two sides you multiply. Between sides a and b.

items.q: A triangle has sides a = 9, b = 12 and c = 13. Find the largest angle, m∠C, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
Which is the Law of Sines?
items.e: Each side is paired with the sine of its opposite angle. a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.

items.q: You know two angles and one side of a triangle. Which law should you use?
items.e: With two angles and a side (AAS or ASA), you have a complete side-angle pair: use the Law of Sines. Law of Sines.

items.q: Two lookout towers are 184 m apart. A fire is seen at angles of 67° and 74° from the line joining the towers. How far is the fire from the first tower (the one with the 67° angle), to the nearest meter?
items.e: The third angle is 39°. The side from the first tower to the fire is opposite the 74° angle: d = 184 × sin 74° ÷ sin 39° = 281 m.

items.q: A triangle has sides a = 4, b = 11 and c = 13. Find the largest angle, m∠C, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
Two boats leave the same dock. One travels 12 miles and the other travels 6 miles, and the angle between their paths is 40°. How far apart are they, to the nearest tenth of a mile?
items.e: Law of Cosines: d² = 12² + 6² − 2(12)(6) cos 40°, so d = 8.3 miles.
